title: Criminal Complaint: State of Wisconsin v. Tehrangi N. Chapman

reports.title: Second member of the Milwaukee Police Department charged with misuse of license plate reader system
Criminal Complaint: State of Wisconsin v. Tehrangi N. Chapman

summary:
Milwaukee Police Detective Tehrangi Chapman, a 22-year veteran in internal affairs, was charged Wednesday with felony misconduct in public office and misuse of a GPS device. He admitted using the department's Flock license plate reader system 20 times to track two people, violating policy. He searched one person's plate 17 times from January 2024 to January 2025 and installed a GPS tracker on that person's vehicle. He also searched another person's plate three times in January 2025, listing "training" as the reason. Chapman had led the investigation into another officer's misuse of the same system.

Police Chief Jeffrey Norman said no one is above the law, and Commissioner Krissie Fung called the charges troubling because internal affairs is meant to ensure accountability. Chapman has been suspended since March 13 and is scheduled to appear in court on July 17. Flock Safety said its audit trails help detect rare abuse. Several Wisconsin communities, including Verona, Dane County, UW-Madison police, and Kaukauna, have ended or declined to renew Flock contracts over privacy and misuse concerns.
